product_class: Fungicide seed treatment: triazoles (FRAC 3, e.g. difenoconazole, prothioconazole) or fludioxonil (FRAC 12)
works_because: Protects the seed and seedling from soil-borne and seed-borne Fusarium during emergence
caution: Protects for a few weeks only; it does not prevent later crown rot, stalk rot or head blight

product_class: Foliar triazole fungicide (FRAC 3: prothioconazole, metconazole, tebuconazole), alone or with an SDHI (FRAC 7)
works_because: Lowers head blight and the toxin DON when applied at flowering
caution: The decision depends on the weather at flowering and the variety; a soil finding only says inoculum may be present. Strobilurins (FRAC 11) at this stage can raise DON

product_class: SDHI seed treatment active against sudden death syndrome (FRAC 7: fluopyram, pydiflumetofen)
works_because: Protects young roots from infection by Fusarium virguliforme, which happens early in cool, wet soil
caution: Only useful if the Fusarium found includes F. virguliforme; foliar fungicides do not control this disease

product_class: Seed treatment active against Rhizoctonia: SDHI (FRAC 7: sedaxane, penflufen, fluxapyroxad) or fludioxonil (FRAC 12); azoxystrobin (FRAC 11) in the furrow
stage: On the seed or in the furrow
works_because: Protects seedlings from Rhizoctonia root rot and damping-off
caution: Rhizoctonia groups differ in the crops they attack; in cereals seed treatments only partly suppress bare patch

product_class: Take-all seed treatment (silthiofam, FRAC 38; fluquinconazole, FRAC 3), where registered
works_because: Delays root infection by the take-all fungus in a second or later cereal
caution: Partial control only and few registrations; a break from cereals is the main control. Ammonium nitrogen instead of nitrate also lowers take-all

product_class: Triazole seed treatment (FRAC 3: difenoconazole, tebuconazole)
works_because: Suppresses early infection by the common root rot fungus
caution: Partial suppression only; deep sowing makes common root rot worse

product_class: Fludioxonil seed treatment (FRAC 12)
works_because: Controls Microdochium seedling blight carried on seed and stubble
caution: Does not prevent snow mould later in winter

product_class: Biological soil treatment with the fungus Coniothyrium minitans, a parasite of sclerotia
stage: Worked into the topsoil about three months before sowing
works_because: The fungus destroys Sclerotinia sclerotia in the soil, which lowers inoculum for following host crops
caution: Needs moist soil and time to work; it lowers inoculum but does not remove it

product_class: Foliar white mould fungicide: SDHI (FRAC 7, e.g. boscalid), thiophanate-methyl (FRAC 1) or fluazinam (FRAC 29)
works_because: Protects the flowers, where white mould infection starts
caution: Only pays off when the canopy is dense and the weather at flowering is cool and wet

product_class: Foliar fungicide at pod fill: strobilurin (FRAC 11) with triazole (FRAC 3), or thiophanate-methyl (FRAC 1)
works_because: Lowers pod and stem blight and seed decay
caution: Does not control stem canker; some Diaporthe populations resist strobilurins

product_class: No fungicide reliably controls charcoal rot
caution: Manage it by avoiding drought stress around flowering (lower plant density, irrigation), rotation and less susceptible varieties

product_class: No fungicide controls Verticillium wilt in field crops
caution: Manage it with resistant varieties and long breaks from host crops

product_class: Fungicides do not reliably control anthracnose stalk rot
caution: Manage it with resistant hybrids, rotation and residue management; foliar fungicides act on the leaf blight phase only

product_class: Oomycete seed treatment: metalaxyl or mefenoxam (FRAC 4), ethaboxam (FRAC 22)
works_because: Protects germinating seed from Pythium damping-off in cold, wet soil
caution: Ordinary fungicide seed treatments do not act on oomycetes; some Pythium populations resist metalaxyl

product_class: Oomycete seed treatment at the Phytophthora rate: mefenoxam or metalaxyl (FRAC 4), ethaboxam (FRAC 22), oxathiapiprolin (FRAC 49)
works_because: Protects seedlings from Phytophthora root rot until variety resistance takes over
caution: Works best together with a resistant or tolerant variety

product_class: Mefenoxam or metalaxyl seed treatment (FRAC 4)
works_because: Protects alfalfa seedlings from Phytophthora and Pythium
caution: Does not control Aphanomyces; on wet soils choose a variety resistant to both

product_class: In-season nitrogen fertiliser (sidedress)
stage: When corn is 15 to 30 cm tall
works_because: Supplies nitrogen when the soil holds less nitrate than the crop will need
caution: The 25 mg/kg level is for a sample of the top 30 cm taken in late spring; check the depth and date of this sample before using it

product_class: Starter nitrogen at sowing
works_because: Covers the period in which microbes lock up nitrogen while breaking down carbon-rich residue

product_class: Agricultural lime
works_because: Raises pH, which frees phosphorus and stops aluminium from harming roots
caution: Lime acts slowly; the amount needs a buffer pH test

product_class: Agricultural lime
works_because: Legume root nodules fix less nitrogen in acidic soil; alfalfa is the most sensitive
caution: Lime acts slowly; the amount needs a buffer pH test

product_class: Phosphorus starter placed in a band near the seed
works_because: At this pH phosphorus is quickly bound by the soil; a band keeps it available near young roots
caution: Whether phosphorus is needed at all takes a soil phosphorus test, which this app does not have

product_class: Zinc fertiliser (chelate or sulphate) with the starter
works_because: Zinc is harder for roots to take up in alkaline soil, and these crops are sensitive to it
caution: Confirm with a soil zinc test

product_class: Iron chelate (EDDHA) in the furrow
works_because: Lowers iron deficiency chlorosis on alkaline, calcareous soils
caution: A tolerant variety matters more than the product; the risk also depends on carbonate and salts, which are not checked here

product_class: Manure or compost
works_because: Adds organic matter, which holds water and nutrients and feeds soil life
caution: Builds up over years, not within one season

product_class: Urease inhibitor (NBPT) with urea or UAN left on the soil surface
stage: With each surface application of urea
works_because: Slows the breakdown of urea, so less nitrogen is lost as ammonia before rain moves it into the soil
caution: Urease genes are found in most soils, so this is a weak signal; not needed when urea is injected or worked in

product_class: Nitrification inhibitor (nitrapyrin, DCD) with ammonium or urea nitrogen, or nitrogen split into several doses
stage: With nitrogen applied before or at sowing
works_because: Keeps nitrogen as ammonium for longer, so less is lost as nitrate or N2O in wet soil
caution: Genes show capacity, not activity; the benefit is largest on wet or poorly drained soil

product_class: Rhizobial inoculant for the crop (Bradyrhizobium for soybean, Rhizobium for dry bean, Sinorhizobium for alfalfa)
works_because: Supplies the nodule bacteria a legume needs to fix nitrogen where the crop has not been grown recently
caution: The sequencing here cannot tell whether nodule-forming strains are present

product_class: Copper-based bactericides may work less well here
caution: Copper resistance genes were found in the soil bacteria, not in a pathogen; treat it as a reason to watch how well copper sprays work

product_class: Lower priority for a biofungicide against root disease
works_because: Soil bacteria here carry the gene for DAPG, an antifungal compound linked to natural take-all decline
caution: Presence of the gene does not show that suppression is taking place
